text.tspan: Dallas Office Memo
To:Tom Ulaszek
From:Marty Pennock
Subject:Basic Time Schedules for Manual Generation
cc:Ira Goldstein - ATX
Leonard Tramiel - SUVL
Sam Tramiel - SUVL
Robert Shen - SUVL
Stephen Chan - SUVL
Richard Miller - SUVL
Maxie Smith - SUVL
A good generic guideline for production of service, technical reference, and option kit manuals
produced on the Atari TT030 using PageStream and DynaCADD is as follows:
Text Creation
Text creation for each manual, especially service guides will vary depending upon the type
of input material that is already available. There are three distinct possibilities in this area.
They are:
A. Existing text material from a previous manual on electronic copy that can be used as a
foundation. This involves having a manual on floppy that can be imported into the system
and changed where necessary. This is the best of the three scenarios as far as time is
concerned. Creation of text from this type of input should run 5-10 working days. This
takes for granted that the input from floppy occurs without any difficulties in file transfer.
B. Existing text material from a previous manual on hard copy that can be used as a
foundation. This involves having a manual on paper that can be marked up and entered
into the system with changes where necessary. This is the second best of the three
scenarios as far as time is concerned. Creation of text from this type of input should run
10-15 working days. This takes for granted that other schedules permit full time work on
entering the into the system.
C. Manual text creation from scratch. This involves having to enter the text from scratch
with no information present on paper or floppy that can be used. This is the worst case of
the three scenarios as far as time is concerned. Creation of text from this type of input
should run 15-25 working days. This takes for granted that other schedules permit full time
work on entering the into the system and that base information such as data sheets and
schematics is available.
